presenting: frightened, itching, and more worried about your face than about your blood pressure
cadence: Talkative and anxious. You answer, then ask the doctor a question back.
fallback: …I can't, doctor. Please, just tell me what's happening to me.

dialogue.patient: I've come out in a rash all over, doctor, and my face has swollen up. And I've had diarrhoea on top of it.
Very fast, right after I ate. It was minutes, not hours.
There must have been something in the food. I ate, and not long after I felt awful.
I'm badly allergic to peanuts. A doctor told me that years ago.
Loose stools — three times in the last hour, I could barely get there.
My belly hurts too — like a knife, then a squeezing, over and over. Left side and low down on the left. Eight out of ten. It doesn't spread anywhere.
Pink wheals, bigger than my nail, raised but they don't peel. Back of my neck, my right upper arm, around my mouth, my left ankle, down the back of my neck.
Seven out of ten for the itching. The rash barely hurts — it's the itch I can't stand.
My face is so swollen my eyes have gone narrow. Forehead, both cheeks, and my nose — I can't breathe through it properly.
There's a wheeze when I breathe out. I can breathe, though — I'm not fighting for it.
No, no high noise when I breathe in.
I'm not dizzy now. Not this minute.
…I did go out for a moment, before I came here. I didn't want to say — my family would panic.
I haven't been out of the country at all.
I take metformin for my sugar, twice a day, and paracetamol for my knees when they ache.
